newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Max awaits offer from Australasian Gold.
newsitem.headline: Max awaits offer from Australasian Gold.

text.p: Max Resources Executive Director Mike Langoulant said on Thursday the company was awaiting an offer from Australasian Gold Mines this week for its stake in the Norseman gold project in Western Australia.
"We have had discussions with Australasian Gold Mines and we expect them to give us an offer for our consideration," Langoulant said in a telephone interview.
He said the offer was likely to be a mixture of cash and shares. Max owns about 14 percent of the existing resource base at Norseman, where Australasian Gold Mines is the main stakeholder.
However, Langoulant said Max would not rush into a decision to sell and had other options for the stake, including a sell-down to Intrepid Mining Corporation, in which it holds 28 percent.
Langoulant reiterated that Max intends to sell its gold assets over time as it moves into the fertiliser business, converting chicken waste to organic manure.
"We really have made a decision to sell our gold assets, or to realise the assets at our convenience to maximise their value, without any specific time span," he said.
Max agreed late last year to buy a U.S. fertiliser plant in Ohio and to acquire WRS Europe Ltd, which has an 87 percent stake in a similar plant under construction in France.

Langoulant, clarifying previous comments by a company director, said negotiations were well advanced to buy the assets of WRS Pacific Ltd, a company managed in Perth. WRS Pacific has interests in joint ventures building fertiliser plants in India and Indonesia.
The Indonesian plant is due for commissioning next month and the Indian one should be completed by December, he said.
